blocking.problem:
The initial-seeding rule says "Before the fixpoint, seed the initialiser atoms of every global, mutable or constant, into its slots." PT1 gives alloca only "AV ∋ (X, 0)"; no rule seeds its contents. In contrast, §17.1 says "shadow-stack frames and heap allocations are zero-filled in both builds", and §17.3 requires a zero-filled pushed frame. Because §5 mandates the least fixpoint and exact dispatch domains before N24, these rules omit an observable initial value. Witness:

target datalayout = "e-p:64:64-i64:64-n8:16:32:64"
declare ptr @__bennett_qalloc(i64, i64)
declare void @__bennett_qfree(ptr)
define void @top(i1 %set) {
entry:
  %p = alloca i64
  br i1 %set, label %store, label %read
store:
  store i64 1, ptr %p
  br label %read
read:
  %raw = load i64, ptr %p
  %idx = freeze i64 %raw
  %width = extractelement <2 x i64> <i64 1, i64 3>, i64 %idx
  %h = call ptr @__bennett_qalloc(i64 0, i64 %width)
  call void @__bennett_qfree(ptr %h)
  ret void
}

The only explicitly seeded store is INT(1), so PT6 gives AV(%raw)={1}, freeze copies it and the repaired PT10 correctly derives VS(%width)={3}. Both supplied LLVM 18/23 O0 recogniser runs return accept with precisely those sets. On %set=false, N24 instead supplies zero in %p, N8 removes freeze and N15/N21 select lane 0, so qalloc receives width 1; on true it receives 3. I executed the normaliser output with the repository shadow-stack seed and a width-recording marker harness under clang 18 and 23 at O0 and O3: outputs are respectively width 1/live 0 and width 3/live 0, with exit 0. Both original sources verify and retain the witness through default<O0>. This is a contradiction between the mandatory width-3-only dispatch and the specified successful width-1 execution, not a request to define source LLVM uninitialised memory: conformance is to the zero-filled materialised program, and freeze is present in the source. The same missing initialization also affects zero-filled heap objects.
blocking.fix: In §5.2 replace the initial-seeding paragraph, before the least-fixpoint sentence, with: "Before the fixpoint, seed the initialiser atoms of every global, mutable or constant, into its slots. For each alloca and allocation-site object, also represent every extent whose initial contents are zero under §§17.1/17.3 as a zero-byte initial image; represent a nonconstant extent symbolically over its possible allocated bytes. Subsequent stores union additional possibilities and never erase these initial possibilities. This is an initial image, not a claim that the object remains immutable." Append to PT6: "For a possibly valid load wholly contained in a zero-filled initial extent, include the all-zero value of the load's representation and width, unioned with values from every overlapping store or copy under the existing interval rules. PT8 propagates these initial byte possibilities when copying memory. Zero contributes no ROOT. Region inputs, replayed caller bytes and other nonzero-initialised contents retain their specified sources; this rule does not replace them with zeros." Add the witness to DB/DN/DS with AV(%raw)=AV(%idx)={INT(0),INT(1)}, VS(%width)={1,3}, verdict=accept, and inputs false/true producing widths 1/3 followed by clean free and code 0. A virtual initialization-store expansion during S2 is an equivalent implementation; I recommend the explicit initial-image rule because it also covers loads at different widths and dynamically sized extents. Do not move the problem to a new rejection, precondition or ISA blocker.

blocking.section: §5.2 definition of Copies and PT3/PT4/PT5; §12.6 N21 bitcast packing; §3.4 width dispatch
blocking.problem:
Section 5.2 defines "Copies" as "AV(result) ⊇ AV(operand) lane by lane" and PT3 includes bitcast in "copies (union)". This is false for a bitcast changing lane geometry: its result is assembled from bits of multiple lanes, not a lane-wise value copy. Section 12.6 already requires the actual packing and resegmentation, so the S2 transfer contradicts the specified execution. Witness:

target datalayout = "e-p:64:64-i64:64-n8:16:32:64"
declare ptr @__bennett_qalloc(i64, i64)
declare void @__bennett_qfree(ptr)
define void @top() {
  %a = insertelement <2 x i8> zeroinitializer, i8 1, i32 1
  %b = bitcast <2 x i8> %a to i16
  %width = zext i16 %b to i64
  %h = call ptr @__bennett_qalloc(i64 0, i64 %width)
  call void @__bennett_qfree(ptr %h)
  ret void
}

Here %a is <0,1>. Under the specified little-endian packing, %b=0|(1<<8)=256 and %width=256. Copying source lane values can supply only 0 and 1; it cannot supply 256. The supplied recogniser on both LLVM 18/23 O0 outputs returns accept, retains the two source lane maps on the scalar %b/%width, and reports VS(%width)={0,1}. This is not merely an internal representation detail: §3.4 specialises widths from that domain and omits the successful width-256 case. Independent instcombine on both majors folds qalloc's width to literal 256. The N21 output uses zext/shl/or, and native executions of that materialised output with clang 18/23 at O0/O3 all record one width-256 allocation, clean free and exit 0. PT5's generic instruction to evaluate integer casts elementwise does not resolve the explicit conflicting lane-copy rule or specify how source lanes combine.
blocking.fix: In §5.2 remove bitcast from the unconditional-copy list in PT3 and add this rule to that row: "A bitcast copies lane by lane only when source and destination have identical lane counts and lane bit widths, treating a scalar as one lane. Otherwise use the virtual N21 bitcast expansion of §12.6: pack the source lane bit patterns into its prescribed bit string, then split that string into destination lanes. Compute the output abstract values through the PT4/PT5 transfers of that expansion; finite INT lane sets denote their full Cartesian product, and the K cap applies to each resulting lane. Unknown bits propagate non-handle top through those transfers. Explicit object and ROOT provenance follows the same expansion and remains subject to §6.2; top never substitutes for ROOT. Apply this rule also to constant expressions and the fixed-vscale form, during S2 before verdicts, candidate sets and dispatch domains freeze." Retain N21's execution semantics. Add the full witness to DB/DN/DS with AV(%b)=AV(%width)={INT(256)}, VS(%width)={256}, verdict=accept, and exactly one width-256 allocation followed by clean free/code 0 on LLVM 18 and 23. Add the inverse scalar-to-vector packing probe as a companion. Direct finite bit-string evaluation is an equivalent implementation of this transfer; I recommend the virtual N21 expansion so analysis and execution share the already decided packing rule. Do not classify this finite, valid case as BLK-1 or reject geometry-changing bitcasts.
